title: private-deploy field notes - acme (vpc/on-prem) - daylog
content:
Day log / scratchpad for ACME private deployment (VPC + on-prem edge cluster). Mostly notes-to-self and action items. Informal - will clean up into runbook once stable.

Date: 2026-02-25
Owner: Priya Singh
Site: ACME Corp - primary DC (on-prem) + AWS VPC peering to staging account
Contact: Jacob Lin (ACME infra), slack #acme-private-deploy, phone +1-415-555-0183

High-level status:
- Initial infra prep done in AWS (VPC, subnets, TGW).
- On-prem cluster provisioned (4 x A100 nodes), K8s 1.27.2.
- Installer run attempted 2/24 - failed during cert-sync step (see blocker below).
- Workaround applied: manual cert copy + k8s secret create, installer resumed, later failed on NFS mount permissions.

Open blockers / reminders:
1) Cert sync failure (PD-3187)
   - Symptoms: installer timeout waiting for certs to appear in kube-system namespace.
   - Root cause: customer SFTP appliance has a strict chroot and the SFTP user mapping changed during maintenance. SFTP path mismatch (/exports/redwood -> /exports/private).
   - Temporary fix: scp certs to bastion and kubectl create secret tls redwood-tls -n kube-system --key key.pem --cert cert.pem
   - Next: coordinate with Jacob to provision a stable S3-compatible endpoint (minio) behind VPC instead of SFTP. Ticketed in PD-3187.

2) NFS mount permission issue on on-prem storage
   - Error: cannot mount /var/lib/redwood-data: permission denied (root_squash enforced).
   - Notes: customer storage team enforces root_squash; we require either squash mapping for installer or use a CSI driver that supports fsGroup.
   - Workaround: applied podSecurityContext.fsGroup=1000 for statefulset; confirmed app can write. Not ideal for node-level mounts.
   - Long-term: request storage team to allow specific export with no_root_squash or provide dedicated PV via CSI (recommended).

3) Network routes and MTU
   - Observed packet drops when transferring large model blobs (~>100MB) between VPC and on-prem. Likely MTU mismatch due to VXLAN overlay on customer's edge router.
   - Action: set MTU to 1400 on host interface for model-sync jobs; test shows transfer completes. Need to update installer to detect/report MTU and suggest 1400 if issues.

Install steps (working sequence) - condensed for quick run:
1) Pre-checks on customer side:
   - Confirm kernel >=5.10, docker/containerd supported (we're using containerd 1.8), iptables-nft vs legacy note.
   - Disable SELinux or set to permissive for installer run (customer uses RHEL 8).
   - Ensure ports open: 22 (bastion), 6443 (k8s api), 2379-2380 (etcd if external), 10250 (kubelet), 30000-32767 (NodePort range) - plus ports for model-ssh sync (tcp 9000) and metrics (9100).

2) Networking/VPC prep:
   - Create VPC peering between ACME-staging and our relay VPC. Add route to on-prem CIDR via TGW.
   - Provision NAT for egress from on-prem cluster to fetch model artifacts (or use S3 mirror inside VPC).

3) Installer prerequisites:
   - Create service account and apply RBAC manifest (installer/service-account.yaml).
   - Pre-seed docker registry credentials in secret: kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred -n redwood --docker-server=registry.acme.local --docker-username=deploy --docker-password=<redacted>
   - Ensure KMS/HSM connectivity: customer uses Azure Key Vault; validate network rules allow outbound to vault endpoints.

4) Run installer (current stable branch)
   - ./rdw-install --env acme --kubeconfig ~/.kube/acme --model-storage nfs://10.1.5.12/exports/redwood --cert-source=sftp://bastion/path
   - Watch logs: kubectl -n redwood logs deploy/installer -f

Post-install checks:
- pod status: kubectl get pods -n redwood (expect all ready except autoscaler which will be pending until quota approved)
- model sync: check /var/lib/redwood-data/models on each node, test model load with curl to local health check (/v1/models/<small-model>/health).
- tracing/observability: verify datadog/otel collector can reach ingest endpoints (customer required allow outbound to our collector IP).

Customer environment quirks to remember:
- ACME uses LDAP user mapping on k8s - namespaced service accounts must match LDAP groups. NOTE: RBAC anomalies seen on 2nd day.
- On-prem time drift observed on one node (ntpd not running) - caused statefulset restarts and certificate TTL mismatches. Add ntp/chrony to precheck list.
- HSM: ACME has Thales Luna. We must schedule on-site windows to test KMS integration. HSM team requires IP allowlist and 2FA auth for test keys.

Action items (next):
- [ ] Follow up PD-3187 with ACME SRE and storage team (Jacob) - propose MinIO S3 mirror to replace SFTP (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Update installer to detect MTU and emit warning / auto-suggest 1400 (owner: Riley)
- [ ] Add ntp/chrony check to preflight script (owner: Evelyn)
- [ ] Create runbook section for NFS vs CSI options and recommend CSI as preferred (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Schedule HSM integration window with ACME (owner: Customer + Priya)

Notes to self:
- Keep logs from failed installer runs in /tmp/acme-install-logs-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz - useful for postmortems.
- When hitting cert sync timeouts, check SFTP (or S3) immediately from bastion to eliminate network tunnel issues (scp/openssl s_client).
- For demo, deploy smaller quantized model first to validate end-to-end before syncing 50GB LLM weights.

Misc command snippets (copy-paste):
- kubectl create secret tls redwood-tls -n kube-system --key /tmp/key.pem --cert /tmp/cert.pem
- tar czvf /tmp/acme-install-logs-$(date +%F).tar.gz /var/log/installer /tmp/rdw-install-logs

End of scratchpad. Will convert into cleaned runbook once remaining blockers resolved.
summary: Daylog scratchpad for ACME private deploy: cert sync and NFS permission blockers, MTU transfer fixes, installer steps, action items.
